messages:
incident-bot: Paging — Inference-path latency SLO breach detected. p95=1.1s p99=2.8s (SLO=2s). Streaming tail stalls rising 5% -> 18%.

devon (oncall): acked. I'm on it. any customer reports? :ambulance: 

sara (sre): seeing auth/tokenstore 5xx and configfetch 429s in control-plane. token-fetch timeouts up to 1.2s. configfetch throttles spiking around 03:12 UTC.

ryan (infra): DB metrics: tokenstore DB connections at 98% of pool, CPU 70%. a few queries at p99 ~600ms. suspect connection saturation + retry storms from configfetch fanout.

devon (oncall): mitigation plan:
- enable local cached-token fallback for inference routing (short TTL)
- flip feature flag llm.use_configfetch_fallback -> true for streaming routes
- temporarily relax control-plane rate-limit for internal configfetch (10m)
- scale tokenstore deployment + restart one replica to clear stuck threads
I'll do the flips and scale now. (reacted with :hammer_and_wrench:)

console-bot: action log — featureflag llm.use_configfetch_fallback set to true by devon; tokenstore scaled 3->6 replicas by devon; controlplane rate-limit rule updated (window=10m, burst allowed) by devon.

sara (sre): after flips: p99 down to 1.9s, stalls 12% -> 6%. still some tail spikes in eu-west. logs show a subset of requests still waiting on token fetch (timeout path).

product-ops: customer-impact summary: support ticket C-3021 (ACME) reporting partial streaming replies in EU. ~4 customers affected, most in EU, severity=high. informing CS.

ryan (infra): queued a DB task to increase max_connections and enable per-pod pooled clients. prepping a week patch for connection-pool improvements. short term we've scaled replicas and restarted a few pods.

devon (oncall): temporary mitigation complete. next steps for post-incident:
1) roll back any aggressive featureflag rollout that caused fanout
2) prioritize tokenstore connection pooling hotfix
3) add better configfetch backpressure and coalescing
4) add alerting on tokenstore connection saturation and configfetch 429 rate

miguel (oncall-next): taking handoff at 03:40 UTC. summary pls + outstanding tasks. :white_check_mark:

devon (oncall): Handoff summary -> Root cause: control-plane configfetch fanout + tokenstore DB conn saturation causing increased auth latencies and streaming tail stalls. Mitigations applied: cached-token fallback, featureflag flip, scale tokenstore, relax internal rate-limit. Current status: p99 ~1.85s (below SLO), stalls ~5%. Outstanding: patch pool fix, rollback/adjust rollout, customer follow-up. Logs/commands below.

devon (oncall): commands used:
```
# flip feature flag
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN\" \\
  -d '{"flag":"llm.use_configfetch_fallback","value":true}' \\
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/flags

# scale tokenstore
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/tokenstore --replicas=6

# relax rate limit (internal)
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
... rate-limit: {window: \"10m\", burst: 200}
EOF
```

sara (sre): created incident doc draft: docs/incident/tailwind-tokenstore-2026-03-15.md assigned owners devon+ryan. Tagging @miguel for follow-up postmortem.

miguel (oncall-next): ack. I'll own the follow-ups and customer comms. Please paste any remaining logs or unusual errors in this thread. If SLO regresses I will re-escalate. :eyes:

devon (oncall): final note: if you see p99 climb >2.2s, revert flag and failover traffic to cached-model variant. Handoff complete. (reacted with :raised_hands:)

incident-bot: incident ticket created INC-20260315-42 assigned to devon, ryan, sara; severity=high; status=monitoring.
